publishing.ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml verifies isolated ad-free output; it does not publish Workers. Manual CI dispatch runs the production HTTP health job, not the verify job.
publishing.purge: .github/workflows/cf-purge.yml waits for a release and purges; it is not a publisher. Default remains pages until CF_DEPLOY_TARGET=workers is deliberately configured.
publishing.sourcePublisher: scripts/trend-publish/publish-approved.mjs pushes HEAD:main then verifies production. It has no Worker upload/activation step. Keep it and related source-publishing automations paused until a functioning Workers publishing path is installed.
publishing.beforeMainPush: Disable Pages Git production auto-deploy and check queued builds so the retained rollback deployment cannot be replaced by the changed adapter. Keep Pages project, custom domains, DNS and known-good deployment. No main push is necessary for the first controlled manual release.
publishing.futureAutomation: A separate authorized Workers publisher must build ordinary-visitor output, capture old sitemap before activation, upload with exact GitHub SHA tag, activate a pinned UUID at 100%, reconcile triggers, verify routing, purge, and submit the preserved delta. A green CI result or Git push does not accomplish that.

unresolvedBlockers: Wrangler authentication expired; no valid OAuth session exists according to the coordinator. Authentication must complete before remote inventory/upload. Verify account and exact Worker existence before choosing the bootstrap branch.

Wrangler OAuth and CF_API_TOKEN are different tool inputs. Our activation/purge/IndexNow helpers explicitly require CF_API_TOKEN plus CF_ACCOUNT_ID; do not read or copy OAuth credentials from private files into artifacts.

Production build verification, cache mirroring and final production dry-run passed. The latest QA build/check, HTTP, body, crawl and English/404 checks also passed as reported by the coordinator. Freeze final source/artifact identities before upload; actual upload startup_time_ms remains unverified.
Confirm account's current Workers plan and CPU allowance. Static-cache lookup, Next middleware/rendering and dynamic OG processing are not proven to fit Free 10ms.
Verify existing D1 identity, schema and secret binding privately. Pages bindings/secrets do not automatically transfer to Workers.

Create a reviewed no-routes bootstrap/rollback configuration only if the Worker is genuinely new. Never run the bootstrap command against an existing unrelated Worker.

permissions.wrangler: Authenticated account access to Workers scripts/versions/deployments and route updates; zone read/route edit for both exact host routes; D1 access only for the selected database operations.
permissions.postRelease: CF_API_TOKEN with Worker deployments/versions read and zone cache purge, plus CF_ACCOUNT_ID and CF_ZONE_ID. Do not store token values in this plan.
permissions.secretHandling: Use masked interactive input or a short-lived owner-only secrets file outside the repository/staging/artifact directories. Do not pass secret values in argv, logs, screenshots, JSON evidence or NEXT_PUBLIC_*.

commandsNotation: All commands below are proposals, NOT EXECUTED. argv arrays are exact arguments, not shell strings. Replace ${...} only with validated coordinator inputs. Use the installed Node CLI paths; do not use npx @latest or update dependencies during release.

Verify fresh .artifacts/production-worker-verification.json and its matched BUILD_ID/chunks. Record all final artifact hashes and cache/assets count after population.

steps.conditions: Worker exists, final preflight passed, and no concurrent uploads/settings changes. Private file contains only FEEDBACK_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET (at least 32 characters) and is outside repo/stage/artifacts with owner-only access. OpenNext runWrangler currently uses shell:true: its passthrough path and release tag must contain no whitespace or shell metacharacters. Do not place a secret value in argv.

steps.semantics: Installed OpenNext upload first populates cache then calls Wrangler versions upload. Wrangler writes annotations['workers/tag'] from --tag, uploads ASSETS and D1 binding metadata, and keeps existing secrets. Upload does not reconcile routes or activate the version.
steps.after: Capture returned full version UUID and startup_time_ms. Read metadata privately to verify exact tag, expected bindings/secret name, compatibility settings, assets and disabled preview state. Ensure the current active deployment is unchanged.

steps.when: Alternative to --secrets-file only; do not run both without reason. Upload the application inactive first, then use masked interactive input.
steps.caveat: This command patches the LATEST uploaded version, not a supplied base UUID. Freeze other uploads and verify latest UUID is the intended application immediately before use. It returns a NEW version UUID. Use that new UUID as CF_EXPECTED_VERSION_ID and verify code/bindings/tag again. Never use plain secret put here because it deploys immediately.

rollback.firstCutover: Restore the recorded Worker route state only. For a verified new Worker with no prior routes, remove only the two newly created route IDs; keep Pages custom-domain/DNS mapping and its known-good deployment, D1 data and Worker versions. Never delete the Pages project or database.

rollback.alternative: A reviewed minimal rollback config containing the same Worker/account, routes:[], workers_dev:false, preview_urls:false can be used with wrangler triggers deploy only when the recorded original route set was empty. It must not remove unrelated routes.
rollback.afterRouteRestore: Verify retained Pages is actually selected and reachable through the canonical domains with guarded non-rendering HTTP. Then run cf-purge-after-deploy.mjs in CF_DEPLOY_TARGET=pages with CF_PAGES_PROJECT=my-salary-calculator and the exact retained CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA. Pages helper only finds a successful matching deployment; it does not restore or prove selected routing.
rollback.laterConditions: Verify the known-good version's own tag/bindings/secret compatibility, then Workers-mode purge with that tag and UUID. Database state is not rolled back by selecting a Worker version. Do not reuse the forward-release IndexNow manifest for a different rollback.

Check raw Total Upload against 64MiB; keep gzip only as historical/informational comparison. Free10ms CPU and startup1s remain independent constraints.

startupVerification.reviewScope: Read-only installed CLI/source and official documentation review; no QA or production artifact was executed for startup profiling.
startupVerification.finding: check startup requires a serialized multipart upload, not worker-entry.js alone. Its local Miniflare profiler measures module initialization, but the default implementation does not guarantee all outbound traffic is blocked. No new harness or CLI execution is authorized by this reporting task.
startupVerification.remainingGate: After authentication and the authorized inactive production versions upload, capture and verify the returned startup_time_ms and upload acceptance before activation. This control-plane result has not been obtained.
startupVerification.limitation: The observed 7.6-second local start-to-first-GET wall time is not startup CPU evidence. Even a local CPU profile would not certify the Cloudflare 1000ms startup limit or Free per-request 10ms allowance.

sizeAndCpu.cpuEvidence: The Next server, middleware/cache JSON work and dynamic OG rendering execute in the Worker. Current code/local wall-time observations do not prove live CPU fits Free10ms. A successful upload also does not prove per-request CPU suitability. Do not silently change caching/security semantics to meet Free.
